subject: ready-for-life
standards: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 1: Home Care Routines That Last
instructions: Complete the task or its stated simulation alternative. Do not submit photos, recordings, addresses, account details, or private household information.
Learner completion never certifies a guardian-authority task; those tasks remain pending until a guardian attests.

learnerTasks.directions: With your adult, pick two real tasks that are clearly different sizes.
learnerTasks.prompt: Name your two tasks and explain what makes one clearly smaller or bigger than the other.

learnerTasks.directions: Before starting either task, write down how many minutes you think each one will take and why.
learnerTasks.prompt: I wrote a specific time estimate in minutes for each task before starting either one.

learnerTasks.directions: Before starting either task, write down how many minutes you think each one will take and why.
learnerTasks.prompt: I gave a reason for each estimate based on the size or steps of the task, not a guess.

learnerTasks.directions: Before starting either task, write down how many minutes you think each one will take and why.
learnerTasks.prompt: My adult reviewed and approved both tasks before I started the timer.

learnerTasks.directions: Time yourself completing each task from start to finish, recording the actual minutes each one took.
learnerTasks.prompt: Record the actual time each task took and the difference between your estimate and the actual time for each one.

learnerTasks.directions: Time yourself completing each task from start to finish, recording the actual minutes each one took.
learnerTasks.prompt: For the task where your estimate was furthest off, explain the specific reason your estimate was too short or too long.

learnerTasks.directions: Compare how close your two estimates were to what actually happened.
learnerTasks.prompt: Explain what you will do differently next time you estimate how long a task will take, based on which of your two estimates today was more accurate and why.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated Estimation reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated Accuracy analysis criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the assessed objective.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Home Care Routines That Last?
